causes.text: Silicon Valley Bank was shut down by regulators on March 10, 2023 after a rapid run on deposits, sparking fears of a broader banking crisis and undermining confidence in the financial sector.

source_info.title: Explainer: What caused Silicon Valley Bank's failure?

causes.text: New York's regulator closed Signature Bank on March 12, 2023 amid a crisis of confidence following SVB's failure, reinforcing contagion concerns across regional lenders.

source_info.title: Signature Bank's closure had 'nothing to do with crypto,' New York regulator says

effects.text: On March 13, 2023, Charles Schwab's shares tumbled about 11.56% as investors feared the brokerage could face liquidity stress similar to regional banks; the sell-off reflected contagion concerns triggered by the bank failures.

source_info.title: Sliding bank shares drag Wall Street down in choppy trade

causal_reasoning_chain.description: In early March 2023, the sudden failure of Silicon Valley Bank led to panicked withdrawals and heightened worries about the solvency of regional lenders.
Shortly thereafter, Signature Bank was shut down amid a crisis of confidence, reinforcing perceptions of systemic weakness in the U.S. banking system.
Investors extrapolated the bank failures to discount brokerages like Charles Schwab, fearing vulnerabilities in sweep deposits and liquidity backstops.
On March 13, 2023, contagion anxiety triggered a sharp sell-off in Schwab's stock, which fell about 11.56% that day as market participants reassessed risk.

rationale: SVB's collapse and Signature's closure undermined confidence beyond regional banks. Parallels with Schwab's sweep-deposit funding model prompted investors to price in elevated liquidity risk, producing a double-digit decline in the shares.
counterfactual_analysis: Absent SVB's failure and Signature's closure, liquidity fears would have been lower, and investor scrutiny of non-bank financials like Schwab would likely have been less acute, reducing the probability of an 11%-plus one-day drop.

adversarial_confounders.text: Broader market volatility and recession fears in March 2023
adversarial_confounders.impact: Risk-off sentiment may have amplified Schwab's decline independent of banking contagion.

details.commentary: OPEC+ production cuts tightened global oil supply, supporting higher prices and cash generation for integrated majors like Chevron. Those stronger cash flows funded dividends and buybacks that attracted more investors, creating a reinforcing loop between commodity prices, shareholder payouts and share-price performance.

Within a concentrated group of large integrated producers, maintaining capital discipline and returning cash became a key way to differentiate. Chevron's willingness to prioritize shareholder payouts in a high-price environment highlighted its competitive positioning, helping it stand out to investors versus peers.
